quantity: kappa* = liminf N0^s(T)/N(T) for zeta, unconditional (new pair-correlation/inertia method)
statement: Theorem A: as T -> infinity, N0^s(T,2T) >= (2/3 - o(1)) N(T,2T) and N_d(T,2T) >= (5/6 - o(1)) N(T,2T). With the Montgomery-Taylor window psi_MT in place of the indicator window, the constants become 2 - c_MT^{-1} = 0.67250... and (3 - c_MT^{-1})/2 = 0.83625.... A fortiori N0*, N0 and N^s are all >= (2/3 - o(1))N. The same holds on (0,T] with rate O(log log T/log T) (Remark 6.1). Theorem B: the same statement holds verbatim for L(s,chi), chi any fixed primitive Dirichlet character. Mechanism: Weil's explicit-formula Hermitian form is restricted to d ~ N(T,2T) modulated copies of a window. Each distinct on-line zero contributes a rank-one positive form, and each off-line pair {rho, 1 - conj(rho)} contributes a block of signature (1,1) (Sylvester inertia). The trace is (1+o(1))N. The squared Hilbert-Schmidt norm is (R(psi)+o(1))N, from Montgomery's prime-side second moment made unconditional by Aryan and by Baluyot-Goldston-Suriajaya-Turnage-Butterbaugh (BGST). A rank-trace inequality rank P1 >= 2 tr P1 + 4 tr Q' - 4b - ||P1+Q'||_HS^2 then gives N0^s >= (2 - R(psi) - o(1))N, with R(flat) = 4/3. No mollifier, zero-density estimate or zero-free region is used.
location: Theorem A and Theorem B, pp. 1-2; mechanism §1.2, eqs. (1.1)-(1.2); Remark 6.1; limits §7.2; Lean statements in Appendix A, p. 15

history.note: secondary source: BCY intro and AF §1.3

caveats: (1) Unrefereed as of 2026-11-17. The paper reports a Lean 4 formalisation (anthropics/zeta-23-lean, tag v1.0, Mathlib 51e6992efd06) whose #print axioms returns only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. We did not re-run it. (2) Dispute about the written proof: J. Arias de Reyna, arXiv:2610.24612 (§1.1 p. 3; footnote 1 p. 15), says that 'as it's written, [v2] doesn't work'. The boundary-zero contribution with U = sqrt(T) is bounded only by O(N), not o(N). He supplies a modified choice, judges the repair to need no more than a note, and asks how a paper with a Lean proof can contain false statements, which suggests the formal object and the printed text differ. No v3 has appeared (arXiv history checked 2026-11-17). (3) The abstract calls 5/12 the previous record for N0^s/N. In fact 5/12 is PRZZ's bound for kappa; their simple-on-line bound is 0.407511. (4) There is an independent human proof (Lamzouri, CRIT-02). (5) The method cannot reach 100% or RH as stated: its inputs are insensitive to o(N) off-line zeros, and they hold for the Davenport-Heilbronn and Epstein zeta functions, for which the analogue of RH fails (§1.4).

quantity: Independent proof of kappa* >= C_MT, plus 'rigidity' bounds (simple OR on the line; average of the two proportions)
statement: Theorem 1.1: liminf N0^s(T)/N(T) >= C0 = 0.67250... and liminf N_d(T)/N(T) >= C1 := (C0+1)/2 = 0.83625.... Moreover liminf N_{s or 0}(T)/N(T) >= C2 = (1 + 2 sqrt2 + 2 C0)/(3 + 2 sqrt2) = 0.88762..., and liminf (N_s(T) + N0(T))/(2N(T)) >= C1. Here C0 = 3/2 - (1/sqrt2) cot(1/sqrt2). Consequences (Remark 1.2): at most 1 - C2 < 0.1124 of the zeros are both off the line and multiple, and max(N0, N_s) >= (C1 + o(1))N. The proof replaces the finite-dimensional matrix and rank-trace framework with a single Hilbert-space inequality, followed by Montgomery's pair-correlation theorem in the unconditional BGST form (Lemma 5 of BGST 2024). The optimisation leads to the same Montgomery-Taylor extremal problem (Remark 3.4).
location: Theorem 1.1 and Remark 1.2, p. 3
caveats: Unrefereed. The author thanks Conrey, Goldston, Gonek, Granville, Milinovich and Tenenbaum for reading a draft, which is not formal refereeing. The Lean certificates were produced afterwards by Axiom Math (Appendix A); we did not check them. This is the main independent human corroboration of CRIT-01. quantity: Computer-assisted refinements: kappa*, N_d/N and N^s/N beyond the Montgomery-Taylor constant
statement: Theorem 1.3: liminf N0^s(T)/N(T) >= s0 = 1669159/2478195 = 0.67353820.... Theorem 1.1: liminf N_d/N >= 1645064/1960733 = 0.83900459675.... Corollary 1.2: liminf N_s/N >= 1329395/1960733 = 0.67800919 (simple zeros anywhere in the strip). Theorem 1.4: (N_s + N0)/(2N) >= 0.83676910 and N_{s or 0}/N >= 0.88916092. Theorem 1.5: N_{s or 0}/N >= 50652159/56956375 = 0.88931500. Method: unconditional pair-correlation 'energy'; a large-sieve inequality for zeros separated by a fixed fraction of the mean spacing; and a computer-assisted local inequality for 7 or 8 consecutive zeros that distinguishes simple from double zeros, with correction terms that telescope as a storage function.
location: Theorems 1.1, 1.3, 1.4, 1.5 and Corollary 1.2, pp. 2-3; method ceilings §7 and Figure 2, pp. 8-9
caveats: (1) Unrefereed, and the bounds are computer-assisted. Lean proofs use three extra axioms, one per local inequality, each recording that a search program returned true; Lean's kernel does not check that run. The paper describes itself as an experiment in AI-assisted research. (2) It lists a swarm of unverified, unrefereed values for kappa* between 0.67300 and 0.673492 (GitHub repos, Zenodo drafts, the Riemann.fail list with Lean entries up to 0.67348). The largest, 0.673492, is a draft pull request (PR 888) to GettysburgResearch/riemann, the host repository of this Observatory. Under this project's rules it is an unreviewed branch claim and must not be counted as a result. (3) A Zenodo report by H. Yang and S. Yang claims 0.7962 simple-on-line and 0.8981 distinct from trace moments of order up to 6. Its own authors grade the analytic part as not yet verified, so it is excluded. (4) The author's earlier paper arXiv:2609.33043 proved N_d/N >= 0.8369928814 (relying on an unrefereed computer-assisted local inequality). (5) B. Wang's arXiv:2609.24167 (+6.67e-8) is withdrawn.

quantity: kappa (zeros on the line, with multiplicity) and kappa*: best REFEREED result, Levinson-Conrey mollifier method

quantity: Disputed constant: Feng's kappa >= 0.4128 (and the earlier claim 0.4173)
statement: Feng (J. Number Theory 132 (2012)) proves Theorem 1: kappa >= 0.4128, using a two-piece mollifier with a Conrey piece of length theta = 4/7 - eps and Feng pieces of length theta1 = 1/2 - eps (I = 3, R = 1.3025). Corollary 1 states that the 'theta = 1' conjecture implies kappa >= 0.6107. Dispute: arXiv v1 of Feng's paper took all pieces of length 4/7 and claimed kappa > 0.4173 and kappa* > 0.4075. After Conrey queried this, Feng accepted the error and reduced the pieces to 1/2 (Bui, arXiv:1410.2433, Remark 1.1). BCY 2011 could not verify that Feng's mollifier may have length 4/7. With only the Balasubramanian-Conrey-Heath-Brown twisted second moment, the cross term needs theta1 + theta2 < 1, which gives theta2 < 3/7 and kappa >= 0.410725, kappa* >= 0.403211 (Kühn-Robles-Zeindler, J. Number Theory 174 (2017), Theorem 1.2). Resolution: Pratt-Robles (2018) proved that the Feng piece may have length 6/11 > 1/2, validating 0.4128 and giving 0.41491637. PRZZ (2020) then proved length 4/7 for the generalised Feng mollifier and recovered essentially Feng's v1 numbers (0.417293962 and 0.407511457). PRZZ §5 also notes that Feng's assertion that non-square-free terms contribute only lower order was an 'unproved claim'; they prove it in §5.1.

quantity: Admissible mollifier length theta (y = T^theta) in the twisted second moment of zeta
statement: Unconditional admissible lengths for the twisted second moment int |zeta(1/2+it)|^2 |A(1/2+it)|^2 dt. Arbitrary coefficients a_n << n^eps: theta < 1/2 (Balasubramanian-Conrey-Heath-Brown 1985), improved to theta < 17/33 (Bettin-Chandee-Radziwill, Crelle 729 (2017) 51-79, via Bettin-Chandee trilinear Kloosterman bounds); Robles-Roy-Zaharescu get 48/95 by bilinear bounds. Conrey-type coefficients mu(n) P(log(y/n)/log y): theta < 9/17 (BCHB, Weil bound) and theta < 4/7 (Conrey 1989, Deshouillers-Iwaniec). Feng-type coefficients mu * Lambda^{*k}: theta < 6/11 (Pratt-Robles 2018, Theorem 1.2, via Type I/II decomposition and incomplete Kloosterman sums), then theta < 4/7 (PRZZ Theorem 4.1, using Vaughan/Heath-Brown identities). PRZZ remark (§9(3)) that additivity of log in (mu * log) is what allows 4/7, and ask how to lengthen without over-specialising the coefficients.
location: PRZZ §1, pp. 7-8 and Theorem 4.1; Pratt-Robles Theorem 1.2, Remark 1.3 and §5 (kappa >= .41491637)
caveats: The values for BCHB (9/17), Conrey (4/7), BCR (17/33) and RRZ (48/95) are as reported in PRZZ's full text (secondary relative to the original papers, except that BCR's journal data were confirmed via zbMATH). No admissible theta > 4/7 for any mollifier that is useful for Levinson's method is known unconditionally; the 4/7 barrier has stood since 1989. Pratt-Robles corrected a misprint in the statement of their Theorem 1.2 in later arXiv versions (it was found by Heath-Brown).

In families the asymptotic large sieve makes theta = 1 available on average. Conrey-Iwaniec-Soundararajan, Theorem 1: for (log Q)^6 <= T <= (log Q)^A, N0'(T,Q) >= (14/25) N(T,Q) for the family of primitive Dirichlet L-functions, where N0' counts simple zeros on the line (kappa' = 0.56001 at theta = 1, r = 10/9, R = 0.83). The mollifier route is therefore dominated unless theta can be pushed well beyond 1. quantity: Limits of mollification as theta grows (theta = infinity, lower bounds for mollified error)
statement: Radziwill, Theorem 1: there is an absolute constant c > 0 such that for every theta > 0, all large T and every M_theta(s) = sum_{n <= T^theta} a(n) n^{-s} with a(n) << n^eps and a(1) = 1, I(M_theta) = (1/T) int_T^{2T} |1 - zeta M_theta(1/2+it)|^2 dt >= c/theta. For theta < 1/2, c = 1 (Proposition B, Soundararajan). Theorem 2: under RH and the Pair Correlation Conjecture, I(M_theta) >= (1 + o_theta(1))/(0.5 + theta). Related: Farmer's 'theta = infinity conjecture' (Mathematika 40 (1993) 71-87) asserts that the Conrey mollifier keeps I ~ 1/theta for all theta and implies 100% of zeros on the line. Bettin-Gonek (Mathematika 63 (2017) 29-33) show that theta = infinity implies RH. Feng (2012, §1 remark (a)) notes that a positive proportion of zeros of zeta + zeta'/log T lie near the line under the small-gap conjecture, so 100% via Levinson needs R -> 0 or a different f(s).
value: I(M_theta) >= c/theta (unconditional); >= 1/(0.5 + theta) under RH + PCC
location: Theorem 1 and Theorem 2, Proposition B, pp. 1-2 (arXiv v3)
caveats: We could not locate a journal publication of Radziwill's paper (zbMATH lists only arXiv:1207.6583). Farmer's and Bettin-Gonek's statements come from secondary sources (Feng intro; PRZZ §1); zbMATH confirmed their bibliographic data only. Conrey-Farmer-Kwan-Lin-Turnage-Butterbaugh (arXiv:2508.11108, abstract) show that optimising the linear combination of derivatives gives a positive proportion for any mollifier length, however short. For short mollifiers this matters more than refining the mollifier. Dong-Wattanawanichkul-Zaharescu (arXiv:2605.24363, abstract) extend Bettin-Gonek to GL(m) automorphic L-functions.

source.venue: arXiv preprint (zbMATH indexes only the arXiv version)

quantity: Ceiling of the pair-correlation / rank-trace (bandwidth-one) method for kappa* and N_d/N
statement: Alpöge-Furman §7.2. A 'bandwidth-one certificate' depends on the configuration only through its first two trace moments against test functions with Fourier support in [-1,1] and through the split into on-line points and off-line pairs, and it satisfies p <= N0^s/N configuration by configuration. For any such certificate p <= p0 + 2.55e-6 (|r'(1)| + int|r''|) for band-limited windows, with p0 <= 0.6818287. This value is the exact rational of an explicit 256-periodic law, certified by interval arithmetic (EnclOK, not kernel-checked) plus Lean-checked inequalities. It is below 0.6819 for both windows used, so 2/3 is within 0.016 of the ceiling. Given only the trace, Hilbert-Schmidt norm and block structure, inequality (1.1) is sharp, and the extremal configuration is Montgomery's: 2N/3 simple on-line zeros plus N/6 doubles. The Montgomery-Taylor window is optimal among windows of the form 2 - R(psi) [CCLM17, Cor. 14]. Unconditionally, higher traces add nothing: the prime-side evaluation of tr G^k is available only for X^k <= T^{2-eps}. Conditionally, the hypothesis HL*(4) (Hardy-Littlewood-type additive correlations) would give kappa* >= 13/18, and HL*(k0) for all k0 would give 100%. Knausgård (§7 and Figure 2) gives ceilings for his refinement: inequalities for 8 consecutive points cannot exceed 0.67357; no pair-energy lower bound for simple points exceeds 0.67383 (Prop. 7.3, second window); any window satisfying V(f) <= 10 B(f) is capped at 0.68185 (Cor. 7.9). For distinct zeros the caps are 0.83916 (7 points), 0.83998 (any frame length) and 0.84093 (any regular window).
location: Alpöge-Furman §1.4 and §7.2 (a)-(f), pp. 12-14; Knausgård §7.3-7.6, Proposition 7.2, Proposition 7.3, Corollary 7.9, Figure 2 (pp. 8-9)
caveats: These are rigorous-computation claims (interval arithmetic and Lean) inside unrefereed preprints. They bound the METHOD, not the true proportions. 'Bandwidth one' corresponds to Montgomery's F(alpha) being known only for |alpha| <= 1. For X >> T the off-diagonal prime sum needs prime-pair (Hardy-Littlewood) information, which Goldston-Montgomery show is equivalent to pair correlation beyond support 1. The two papers' ceilings agree (0.6818287 vs 0.68185).

quantity: Proportion of simple zeros of zeta under RH (and GRH / GLH)
statement: Bui-Heath-Brown, Theorem: assuming RH, kappa* >= 19/27 (here kappa* = liminf N*(T)/N(T), N* counting simple zeros). Corollary: on RH, kappa_d >= 0.84665. This removes the Generalised Lindelöf Hypothesis from Conrey-Ghosh-Gonek (Proc. LMS 76 (1998) 497-522), using Heath-Brown's generalised Vaughan identity. Method: Cauchy-Schwarz on the first and second mollified discrete moments of zeta'(rho) over zeros. Pair-correlation route under RH (Chirre-Gonçalves-de Laat, Adv. An unconditional version of the CGG/BHB discrete-moment method would therefore beat that ceiling. RH enters BHB through the evaluation of sums over zeros as sums over real ordinates. statement: Baluyot-Goldston-Suriajaya-Turnage-Butterbaugh (arXiv:2501.14545v3, Theorems 1-2): if for all large T every zero with T < gamma <= 2T satisfies |beta - 1/2| < b/(2 log T), then N0^s(B_0.3185) >= (0.66666908 + o(1)) (T/2pi) log T, which recovers the 2/3 proportion. Goldston-Lee-Schettler-Suriajaya (arXiv:2503.15449, abstract): Montgomery's Pair Correlation Conjecture alone, without RH, implies that asymptotically 100% of zeros are simple and on the critical line (Gallagher-Mueller method plus 'horizontal multiplicity'). The same holds under a form of the Alternative Hypothesis (arXiv:2507.06823). BGST 2024 (Acta Arith. 214, 357-376): if all zeros with T^{3/8} < gamma <= T lie within 1/(2 log T) of the line, at least 61.7% are simple.

source.title: More than 83.9% of the zeros of the Riemann zeta function are distinct and more than 67.35% are simple and on the critical line

quantity: Proportion of zeros that are simple OR on the critical line, unconditional
statement: Lamzouri Theorem 1.1 gives liminf N_{s or 0}/N >= 0.88762. Cobeli-Zaharescu, Theorem 1: liminf N_{s or 0}(T)/N(T) > 8/9; the proof gives about 0.88893 (eq. (6.2)). Knausgård Theorem 1.5: >= 50652159/56956375 = 0.88931500 (computer-assisted). Under the narrow-box hypothesis, BGST Theorem 3(iii), after an observation of Soundararajan, gives (2 + C0)/3 = 0.89083.
location: Theorem 1, p. 2 and eq. (6.2); Knausgård Theorem 1.5, p. 3; Lamzouri Theorem 1.1
caveats: All unrefereed. Cobeli-Zaharescu do not cite Knausgård's earlier (6 Oct 2026) and larger computer-assisted value 0.889315. A consequence: at most about 11% of zeros can be both off the line and multiple.

source.title: More than 8/9 zeros of the Riemann zeta function are simple or on the critical line

quantity: Proportion of c-isolated zeta zeros (isolated implies simple and on the line), unconditional
statement: Theorem 1.1: let B0(T,c) count the zeros rho_n with min(gamma_{n+1} - gamma_n, gamma_n - gamma_{n-1}) > 2 pi c/log T. There is c > 0 with liminf B0(T,c)/N(T) >= 0.6552, and liminf B0(T,1/6)/N(T) >= 0.50875. Before this it was not known unconditionally that infinitely many isolated zeros exist. The method is an unconditional variant of Montgomery's pair-correlation method. The same paper shows at least 31% of zeros of a linear combination of two primitive Dirichlet L-functions with the same conductor and parity lie on the line with odd multiplicity; the previous value was 7.38e-9 (Dousselin).
caveats: Unrefereed. The author did not optimise the small-c proportion (Remark 1.2). This is qualitatively stronger than kappa*, since isolated zeros are simple and on the line.

source.title: Isolated zeros of the Riemann zeta function and zeros of linear combinations of Dirichlet L-functions

quantity: Explicit kappa from Selberg's sign-change method (and correction of Zhuravlev's 1974 constant)
statement: Theorem 1.1: more than 6.78% of the nontrivial zeros of zeta lie on the critical line; precisely kappa_0 > 0.0678190. The method is a mollified Selberg sign-change detector with coefficients lambda(n) of zeta^{-1/2} with profile powers v^{1/4} and v, plus rigorous interval computation (0.6779054 < C_{1/4} < 0.6786576). Correction: Zhuravlev's 1974 paper prints 2/21, but its logarithmic inequality drops a factor of 2 and its polar term has the wrong sign. The corrected benchmark is 2/(3 pi^2 e) = 0.0248493202 (eq. (4)).
location: Theorem 1.1, p. 1; eq. (4) and discussion, p. 2; §2.4 (Baluyot's Atkinson-type bound)
caveats: v2 itself corrected the proportion stated in v1 (we did not retrieve v1's value). The result is far below Levinson-type bounds; its interest is for L-functions where Levinson's method is unavailable. Baluyot's Atkinson-type method gives kappa_0 > 0.0001049 (0.0086729 if his fourth-moment estimates hold for mollifiers of any length), as reported there.

source.title: Optimising Selberg's method for critical zeros

quantity: Critical and simple zeros of Dirichlet L-functions (individual and family averages)
statement: Individual fixed primitive chi: Alpöge-Furman Theorem B gives N0^s >= (2/3 - o(1))N, or 0.6725 with the MT window (unrefereed). Wu (Math. Z. 293 (2019) 825-865, abstract) proves, for every Dirichlet L-function, more than 41.72% of zeros on the line and more than 40.74% simple and on the line by Levinson-Conrey with a longer mollifier. Families: Conrey-Iwaniec-Soundararajan show at least 14/25 simple on the line for (log Q)^6 <= T <= (log Q)^A; Sono (abstract) gets 61.07% / 60.44%. Alpöge-Furman Remark 7.2 gives family averages of 0.811 simple-on-line and 0.905 distinct with smooth weights, details omitted and not formalised. Hua-Yang (arXiv:2608.16034, abstract) prove C_MT for the unweighted prime-modulus family at low heights. Under GRH, Chandee-Lee-Liu-Radziwill (arXiv:1211.6725, abstract) show 91% simple.
value: 0.6725 (each fixed chi, unrefereed); 41.72% / 40.74% (each chi, refereed); 14/25 to 0.811 (family averages)
location: Theorem B, p. 2; Remark 7.2, p. 14. CIS Theorem 1, eq. (1.5).
caveats: Wu, Sono, Hua-Yang and Chandee-Lee-Liu-Radziwill are abstract-only for us. The 0.811 / 0.905 family values come with omitted details: 'checked by independent derivations but is not included in the Lean formalisation'. Treat them as an announcement. Family results are averages and say nothing about individual members.

source.title: More than two thirds of the zeta zeros are simple and on the critical line

quantity: Critical zeros of GL(2) and GL(3) L-functions (and Epstein zeta)
statement: Andersen-Thorner (Forum Math. 33 (2021) 477-491, abstract): at least 6.96% of the zeros of the L-function of any holomorphic or Maass cusp form lie on the critical line, by Levinson's method with Blomer-Harcos shifted-convolution bounds. Earlier: Hafner 1983 gave a positive proportion for level 1; Rezvyakova extended this to Gamma_0(D) (arXiv:1212.2948); Bernard 2015 and Kühn-Robles-Zeindler gave explicit small proportions. Conrey-Farmer-Kwan-Lin-Turnage-Butterbaugh (arXiv:2508.11108, abstract): optimised linear combinations of derivatives 'more than double' the modular proportions of Bernard and KRZ with the same arithmetic inputs. Conrey-Kwan-Lin-Turnage-Butterbaugh (arXiv:2607.00282, abstract): at least 1/9 of zeros of L(s, Pi_0 x chi), Pi_0 on PGL(3), averaged over primitive chi of conductor up to Q, lie on the line (unconditional for self-dual Pi_0). Rezvyakova (arXiv:2411.18492, abstract): Epstein zeta functions of integral binary forms have a positive proportion of zeros on the line.
location: Main theorem (abstract)
caveats: Abstract-level only. Alpöge-Furman's bandwidth-one pair-correlation argument might plausibly extend to GL(2), but no such statement was found in the sources read. Pair correlation for GL(2) at bandwidth one is a separate input. Epstein zeta violates RH, so a positive proportion there shows that the critical-line count does not detect RH.

source.title: Zeros of GL_2 L-functions on the critical line

quantity: Unrefereed claims of 100% (or much larger) proportions: not accepted
statement: Preobrazhenskaya-Preobrazhenskii, arXiv:1805.07741v7 (math.GM, 1 Nov 2025), state 'Theorem 1. kappa = 1' (almost all zeros on the critical line). The approach is a Levinson-type method applying the AM-GM inequality and second-moment asymptotics only on a subset, with zero-density exponents of Jutila and Conrey and a Schwarz-Christoffel mollifier. Dumitrescu-Wolf, arXiv:2205.09042 (abstract), also claim almost all zeros are on the line. H. Yang and S. Yang (Zenodo 2026, cited by Knausgård) claim 79.62% simple-on-line.
location: Theorem 1, §1 (v7)
caveats: We read only the statement and abstract and did not audit the proof. Grounds for not accepting it: (a) seven versions over 2018-2025, listed in math.GM; (b) every 2026 paper read (Alpöge-Furman, Lamzouri, Knausgård, Pearce-Crump, Arias de Reyna) treats PRZZ's 5/12 as the unconditional record before August 2026; (c) Feng's remark (a) and Radziwill's c/theta bound (CRIT-09) show that Levinson-type arguments at finite length cannot simply be pushed to 100%. Listed only so that the ledger records these claims; do not cite them as results.

source.title: Almost all of the zeros of the Riemann zeta-function are on the critical line

quantity: Existence and range of the de Bruijn–Newman constant Λ (classical ζ)
statement: Normalization used throughout this ledger (Polymath/Rodgers–Tao): H_t(z) = ∫_0^∞ e^{tu²} Φ(u) cos(zu) du, Φ(u) = Σ_{n≥1} (2π²n⁴e^{9u} − 3πn²e^{5u}) exp(−πn²e^{4u}), H_0(z) = (1/8) ξ(1/2 + iz/2). H_t solves the backward heat equation ∂_t H_t = −∂_zz H_t. Pólya: if H_t has only real zeros, so does H_{t'} for every t' > t. de Bruijn (1950): H_t has only real zeros for t ≥ 1/2. Newman (1976): there is an absolute constant Λ with −∞ < Λ ≤ 1/2 such that H_t has only real zeros if and only if t ≥ Λ. RH ⇔ Λ ≤ 0. Newman conjectured Λ ≥ 0, which he called a quantitative version of the dictum that RH, if true, is only barely so.
location: Newman 1976, main theorem, as restated in Rodgers–Tao arXiv:1801.05914v5 §1 p.2. de Bruijn 1950 Thm 13, as restated in Dobner arXiv:2005.05142 Thm 3 p.9.
caveats: I could not read the original PDFs because the AMS site returned a bot-check page. Watch the normalization: Ki–Kim–Lee (zbMATH 1175.30023) use Ξ_λ with Λ = 4λ^(0), and other papers use t/4 conventions. Every number in this ledger is in the H_t normalization above.

source.authors: C. M. Newman; N. G. de Bruijn
source.title: Fourier transforms with only real zeros (Proc. AMS 61 (1976) 245–251); The roots of trigonometric integrals (Duke Math. J. 17 (1950) 197–226)
source.venue: Proc. Amer. Math. Soc.; Duke Math. J.

quantity: de Bruijn strip contraction (how an initial zero strip turns into an upper bound for Λ)
statement: Let φ be even and integrable with φ(u) = O(e^{−|u|^b}) for some b > 2, G(z) = ∫ φ(u) e^{izu} du, and G_t(z) = ∫ e^{tu²} φ(u) e^{izu} du. If every root of G lies in |Im z| ≤ Δ, then for t > 0 every root of G_t lies in |Im z| ≤ max(Δ² − 2t, 0)^{1/2}. Hence Λ ≤ Δ²/2. The classical strip 0 < Re ρ < 1 gives Δ = 1 and so Λ ≤ 1/2. A zero-free half-plane Re s > σ, combined with the functional equation, gives Δ = 2σ − 1 and so Λ ≤ (2σ−1)²/2. For σ = 7/8 this is Λ ≤ 9/32 = 0.28125 (Hakimoglu-Brown §1.1). My own arithmetic: σ = 11/12 gives Λ ≤ 25/72 ≈ 0.347, and beating 0.2 by this step alone would need σ ≤ (1+√0.4)/2 ≈ 0.8162.
value: Λ ≤ Δ²/2 for an initial zero strip of half-width Δ
location: de Bruijn 1950 Thm 13, as restated in Dobner arXiv:2005.05142 Thm 3 p.9. Used as Polymath arXiv:1904.12438 Thm 3.2. The σ = 7/8 conversion is in Hakimoglu-Brown arXiv:2610.12803 §1.1 p.2.
caveats: I did not open de Bruijn's original. The statement is quoted from Dobner's full text.

source.title: The roots of trigonometric integrals

quantity: Strict upper bound Λ < 1/2 and asymptotic reality of zeros for t > 0
statement: Ki–Kim–Lee: Λ < 1/2, and for every t > 0 all but finitely many zeros of H_t are real and simple. Polymath later made this uniform (arXiv:1904.12438 Thm 1.5). For 0 < t ≤ 1/2, with C a sufficiently large and c a sufficiently small absolute constant: if x ≥ exp(C/t) and H_t(x+iy) = 0, then y = 0 and x = x_n + O(x^{−ct}) for some n. The function g(x,t) = (x/4π)log(x/4π) − x/4π + 11/8 + (t/16)log(x/4π) counts the zeros.
value: Λ < 1/2. For t > 0, H_t has only finitely many non-real zeros.
location: KKL main theorem and Theorems 1.3–1.4 (per zbMATH 1175.30023 and Polymath p.10). Polymath Thm 1.5, arXiv:1904.12438v2 pp.9–10 (full text read).

history.value: effective-form uniform version (Thm 1.5); explicit bound Λ ≤ 0.22

caveats: Secondary sources give only the strict inequality; I verified no explicit margin δ in Λ ≤ 1/2 − δ, and Rodgers–Tao call it 'sharpened slightly'. The constant C in Polymath Thm 1.5 is not explicit. The 2026 collision-exclusion claims use Thm 1.5(i) only in its qualitative form (remote reality).

source.authors: H. Ki, Y.-O. Kim, J. Lee
source.title: On the de Bruijn–Newman constant

quantity: Zero dynamics of H_t under the backward heat flow (Csordas–Smith–Varga)
statement: For Λ < t (in particular Λ < t ≤ 0 if Λ < 0), the zeros of H_t are real, simple and avoid 0 (CSV Cor. 1). The positive zeros satisfy ∂_t x_k = 2 Σ_{j≠k} 1/(x_k − x_j) (CSV Lemma 2.4). This is a repulsion: zeros spread apart as t increases. A negative Λ would therefore forbid sufficiently close adjacent zeros ('Lehmer pairs') at t = 0, and the CSV criterion (Thm 1) turns a high-quality Lehmer pair into a lower bound for Λ. Polymath Prop. 3.1 extends the ODE to every simple complex zero at every t (symmetric-pair summation). A zero of multiplicity m ≥ 2 at t0 splits as z_j(t0) + √2 (t−t0)^{1/2} λ_j + O(|t−t0|), where λ_j are the roots of the Hermite polynomial He_m. CSV's own lower bound is Λ > −4.379×10⁻⁶.
value: ∂_t x_k = 2 Σ' 1/(x_k − x_j); CSV lower bound Λ > −4.379×10⁻⁶
location: CSV Cor. 1, Lemma 2.4 and Thm 1, as cited in Rodgers–Tao arXiv:1801.05914v5 pp.3–5 and p.11. Polymath arXiv:1904.12438v2 Prop. 3.1 pp.12–13 (full text).
caveats: The zbMATH review text is unavailable because of licensing, and I did not read the CSV original. The ODE as written is the Polymath/Rodgers–Tao version.

source.authors: G. Csordas, W. Smith, R. S. Varga
source.title: Lehmer pairs of zeros, the de Bruijn–Newman constant Λ, and the Riemann hypothesis

quantity: Lower bound on Λ before Newman's conjecture was proved (Lehmer-pair method)
statement: Found a new Lehmer pair of ζ zeros, which gives Λ > −1.14541×10⁻¹¹. This was the record lower bound until Rodgers–Tao proved Λ ≥ 0.
location: Abstract/main result (zbMATH 1267.11094 summary). Rodgers–Tao arXiv:1801.05914v5 Table 1 p.3.
caveats: The secondary sources disagree on one row. Rodgers–Tao Table 1 lists Odlyzko 2000 as −2.63×10⁻⁹, while the zbMATH review 0967.11034 of Odlyzko's paper says −2.7×10⁻⁹. Odlyzko's PDF failed TLS verification, so I could not settle it. Rodgers–Tao round SGD to −1.15×10⁻¹¹. I did not examine the rounding model of these published Lehmer-pair computations. All of these bounds are superseded by DBN-06.

source.authors: Y. Saouter, X. Gourdon, P. Demichel
source.title: An improved lower bound for the de Bruijn–Newman constant

quantity: Newman's conjecture for ζ: lower bound Λ ≥ 0
statement: Theorem 1: Λ ≥ 0. Combined with RH ⇔ Λ ≤ 0, this gives RH ⇔ Λ = 0. The proof is by contradiction. Assuming Λ < 0 (and RH, which is harmless for this purpose), the CSV dynamics on Λ/4 ≤ t ≤ 0, together with Riemann–von Mangoldt-type counts for H_t and a Hamiltonian/energy monotonicity (∂_t H = −4E for the formal gradient flow), force the zeros of H_0 into local equilibrium. Concretely, x_{j+1}(0) − x_j(0) = (4π + o(1))/log T for a fraction 1 − o(1) of j ∈ [T log T, 2T log T]. This contradicts the Conrey–Ghosh–Goldston–Gonek–Heath-Brown small-gap theorem: for any λ > 0.77, a positive proportion of gaps are ≤ λ·4π/log T. Montgomery's pair correlation would also suffice.
location: Theorem 1, p.3 (arXiv v5). Contradiction step in §9, pp.59–60. Section 8 energy estimates, footnote 16 p.55.

history.value: independent proof; extended to the extended Selberg class

caveats: Erratum-type note: arXiv v5 (3 Jul 2021) says it is 'the published version, but with some corrections to Section 8' after Ofer Zeitouni pointed out that the treatment of boundary contributions to the energy was inadequate (footnote 16 p.55). Crossref shows no registered erratum on 10.1017/fmp.2020.6 (checked 2026-11-17). Dobner's independent proof (DBN-07) makes the conclusion robust. Separately, an unrefereed preprint (A. Gershon, Preprints.org, 22 Apr 2026, doi 10.20944/preprints202604.1513.v1, 'The De Bruijn-Newman Constant Is Zero') claims Λ = 0, which is equivalent to RH. I read only its abstract. It is unverified and not accepted, and RH remains open.

source.title: The de Bruijn–Newman constant is non-negative

quantity: Generalized Newman conjecture: Λ_F ≥ 0 for every F in the extended Selberg class S♯
statement: Thm 1: for every F ∈ S♯ there is a real number Λ_F such that all zeros of ξ_t^F lie on the critical line iff t ≥ Λ_F. Thm 2: Λ_F ≥ 0 for every F ∈ S♯. This includes ζ and every primitive Dirichlet L-function. The proof uses no information about ζ zeros. For each t < 0, ξ_t(J_t(s)) ≈ [gamma-like factor]·ζ_t(s) with ζ_t(s) = Σ exp((t/4) log² n) n^{−s} (Thm 4), and a Bohr-type almost-periodicity theorem then shows that ξ_t has infinitely many zeros off the critical line.
value: Λ_F ≥ 0 for all F ∈ S♯; for t < 0 there are infinitely many off-line zeros
location: Theorems 1–2, p.3. Theorem 3 (de Bruijn), p.9. Theorem 4 and §3.1 (deduction of Thm 2).

history.value: framework for automorphic and function-field analogues

caveats: S♯ requires a Dirichlet series, meromorphic continuation and a functional equation, but no Euler product. This number-field setting differs from function fields, where individual Λ_D can be −∞ (DBN-18). Dobner gives no upper bounds on Λ_F beyond what de Bruijn's strip argument yields.

source.title: A proof of Newman's conjecture for the extended Selberg class

quantity: Polymath15 upper bound Λ ≤ 0.22 and the upper-bound criterion
statement: Thm 1.2 (criterion). Suppose t0, X > 0 and 0 < y0 ≤ 1 satisfy three conditions. (i) ζ(σ+iT) ≠ 0 for (1+y0)/2 ≤ σ ≤ 1 and 0 ≤ T ≤ X/2 (RH verified to height X/2). (ii) H_{t0}(x+iy) ≠ 0 for x ≥ X + √(1−y0²) and y0 ≤ y ≤ √(1−2t0) (canopy). (iii) H_t(x+iy) ≠ 0 for X ≤ x ≤ X + √(1−y0²), √(y0² + 2(t0−t)) ≤ y ≤ √(1−2t), 0 ≤ t ≤ t0 (barrier). Then Λ ≤ t0 + y0²/2. Thm 1.1: Λ ≤ 0.22, obtained with t0 = 0.2, y0 = 0.2, X = 6×10¹⁰ + 83952 − 0.5 and Platt's interval-arithmetic RH verification to 3.06×10¹⁰. The offset 83952 makes a partial Euler product over p ≤ 11 large. The authors say the canopy (ii) was the numerical bottleneck.
location: Thm 1.1 and Thm 1.2, p.2. Parameter choice §8.1, p.37. Claim verification §8.2–8.5. Effective Riemann–Siegel approximation Thm 1.3.
caveats: The barrier verification used Taylor-expansion 'stored sums' with a 20-decimal-digit target accuracy and conservative derivative bounds (p.48–49). The code is in the arb/ and pari/ directories of github.com/km-git-acc/dbn_upper_bound. I did not replay it.

source.title: Effective approximation of heat flow evolution of the Riemann ξ function, and a new upper bound for the de Bruijn–Newman constant

quantity: Upper bounds on Λ conditional on further RH verification (Polymath Table 1), and the expected 1/log T scaling
statement: Polymath Table 1 lists pairs of a barrier location X and parameters (t0, y0) for which hypotheses (ii) and (iii) of Thm 1.2 were verified numerically, each giving Λ ≤ t0 + y0²/2 provided RH is verified to height X/2. Sample rows: X = 2×10¹²+129093 gives 0.21; X = 5×10¹²+194858 (t0 = 0.186, y0 = 0.16733) gives 0.20; X = 2×10¹³+131252 gives 0.19; X = 6×10¹³+123375 gives 0.18; X = 3×10¹⁴+188911 gives 0.17; X = 2×10¹⁵+122014 gives 0.16; X = 7×10¹⁵+68886 gives 0.15; X = 6×10¹⁶ gives 0.14; X = 6×10¹⁷ gives 0.13; X = 9×10¹⁸ gives 0.12; X = 2×10²⁰ gives 0.11; X = 9×10²¹+70686 gives 0.10. So Λ ≤ 0.1 would follow from RH verified to about 4.5×10²¹. The authors' heuristic is that RH verified to height T gives Λ ≤ O(1/log T). An off-line zero at height T with y ≍ 1 moves at speed ≍ log T, so the bound cannot be improved substantially without excluding RH violations at height T or 'a massive expansion of the known zero-free regions'.
value: Λ ≤ 0.21 … 0.10, depending on the RH verification height (X/2 ≈ 10¹² … 4.5×10²¹)
conditional_on: RH numerically verified up to height X/2 for the chosen row, and correctness of the §10 barrier/canopy computations
location: §10 'Further numerical results': heuristic on pp.62–63, Table 1 'Conditional Λ Results' on p.64, computation remarks on pp.66–67.
caveats: §10 says the mesh points were computed to 20 digits, except for the two highest rows (10 digits), and that the two largest runs used a BOINC volunteer grid. The text does not explicitly state outward-rounded interval enclosures for these rows, so their certification level is less transparently documented than §8. The O(1/log T) scaling is a heuristic, not a theorem. My own arithmetic gives an implied constant t·log X of about 5.0–5.9 across the table.

source.title: Effective approximation of heat flow evolution of the Riemann ξ function, and a new upper bound for the de Bruijn–Newman constant

quantity: Best peer-reviewed unconditional upper bound for Λ (classical ζ)
statement: Theorem 1: RH holds up to height 3,000,175,332,800, verified with interval arithmetic; the first 12,363,153,437,138 non-trivial zeros are on the line. Corollary 2: Λ ≤ 0.2. Row 2 of Polymath Table 1 needs H > 2.51×10¹², and the X in that table corresponds to 2H. The authors note that Λ < 0.19 would need H 'a little higher than 10¹³', and that 'some extra decimals could be wrought out of the calculation' at the achieved H, which they did not pursue.
location: Theorem 1, p.2. Corollary 2, §3.4, p.5. Footnote 2, p.5.

history.authors: Mosaic Intelligence; Gomila; Kornaus; Gordon; Raymond; Planat; Planat–Raymond

caveats: The 0.2 bound depends on Polymath Table 1 row 2 (X = 5×10¹²+194858, t0 = 0.186, y0 = 0.16733), whose canopy and barrier runs are the §10 computations described in DBN-09. As of 2026-11-17, MathWorld and Planat–Raymond both list 0.2 as the last peer-reviewed bound. Mosaic Intelligence (Zenodo 21175533) mentions an uncertified 2020 blog-comment value of 0.1972624050 (R. Dwars), which is secondary only. The harvested metadata contains no later published rigorous RH-verification height beyond 3·10¹².

source.title: The Riemann hypothesis is true up to 3·10^12

quantity: Smallest unrefereed upper bound for Λ that is unconditional in form
statement: Raymond reports Λ ≤ 18674384228461/125000000000000 = 0.149395073827688 < 0.149396 in the Polymath normalization. The proof starts from the classical width-one zero strip at t = 0 and couples a finite-head localisation wall and uniform logarithmic-derivative estimates ('correlated translated probes') to a decreasing zero-height barrier.
location: Zenodo record description (v1.1). Cited as [16] in Planat–Raymond arXiv:2611.06245 Table 1 p.2 and in Planat arXiv:2610.18214 p.2 (0.149395073827688).
caveats: Erratum (deposit v1.1, 30 Oct 2026): the Gaussian remainder constant was corrected from 5/6 to 11/12 and a wall estimate was replaced by 697/900 > 3/4. The author states the bound is unchanged. The work is not peer reviewed, I did not replay it, and Planat–Raymond explicitly decline to treat it as established. Planat (arXiv:2610.18214) reports a slightly smaller ceiling, 0.148611789321711, but only under the extra premises listed in DBN-14.

source.title: Correlated translated probes and the bound Λ < 0.149396 for the de Bruijn–Newman constant
source.venue: Zenodo certificate manuscript, v1.1 with erratum (30 Oct 2026)

quantity: Collision-exclusion upper bound for Λ (unrefereed, full text read)
statement: Claim: Λ < 156821/10⁶ = 0.156821. The only external inputs are Polymath Thm 1.3, eqs. (20)–(24), Thm 3.2 and Thm 1.5(i), plus the Platt–Trudgian height 3,000,175,332,800 and the bound Λ ≤ 1/5. The method excludes collisions of real zeros, meaning simultaneous vanishing of (H_t(x), ∂_x H_t(x)), for all real x and all t ∈ [0.156821, 0.2]. Three regions are handled separately: the compact interior up to a stationary separator at X = 6000000185827, a finite exterior X ≤ |x| ≤ W = 72382294738709 using five stable prime-polynomial Gram sources, and an Euler-product barrier for |x| ≥ W. Remote reality then forces any positive critical time to produce a finite multiple real zero. The certificate uses 664,505 Fourier coefficients, 44,182 torus boxes, 184 separator moments and 17,385 separator rectangles.
location: Eq. (3), p.3. Table 1, p.2. §2.1–2.2, pp.3–4. Certificates in GitHub release certificates-0156821-v1, commit 18dbc01ea36bf9a24d8f79822b5ce06b545e4ace.
caveats: This is a draft that has not been refereed. The authors identify a Cauchy–Schwarz obstruction intrinsic to the four-prime source family, which explains the narrow feasibility margin. Their Table 1 is a useful status classification of the whole 2026 cluster (U/CA/C7/8 and P/R labels). I did not replay any certificate.

source.title: Certified Collision Exclusion and an Unconditional Upper Bound Λ<0.156821 for the de Bruijn–Newman Constant

quantity: Other 2026 unrefereed upper bounds that are unconditional in form
statement: In rough chronological order. Mosaic Intelligence (3 Jul 2026, AI-generated, Zenodo 21175533): Λ ≤ 3/16 = 0.1875 at the Platt–Trudgian/Polymath barrier site, via an Euler-3 mollifier and a ladder 0.1965 → 0.1891 → 0.1875. Gomila (20 Aug 2026, GitHub certificate): Λ ≤ 0.1787854. Kornaus (Sep 2026, Zenodo 22658444): Λ < 0.172422 by collision exclusion. Gordon (SSRN 7608638, Sep 2026): Λ ≤ 0.157656619095490606768… < 0.158, via a piecewise-affine barrier for squared imaginary parts with a 12,666-row rational certificate, ball arithmetic, and a Lean 4 companion that is conditional on stated analytic inputs. Planat (arXiv:2610.32694, Cor. 7.24 eq. (184) p.61): Λ ≤ 433/2500 = 0.1732, using t_e = 0.15653409755 and y_e = 0.18257 with Polymath's published time-barrier rectangle and the Platt–Trudgian finite-RH input, without a quasi-RH assumption. quantity: Upper bounds for Λ conditional on the zero-free half-plane Re s > 7/8 (H7/8)
statement: Hakimoglu-Brown, Theorem 1: if every nontrivial zero of ζ has real part ≤ 7/8, then Λ ≤ 13963/100000 = 0.13963. H7/8 enters only as the initial strip M(0) ≤ 9/16, where M(t) = sup(Im z)² over zeros of H_t. A 24-step strip comparison then uses the Polymath §8.4 boundary computation, a logarithmic-derivative kernel and its vertical derivative at height 61/20. Earlier versions of the comparison gave 0.19388, 0.17973, 0.17172 and 0.16408. Raymond (2026b, Zenodo 23752103) reports Λ ≤ 0.107964910079, taking OpenAI's 7/8 nonvanishing theorem as the initial strip and calling the result 'unconditional'.

caveats: The status of the inputs is disputed. Raymond 2026b describes its bound as unconditional, while Planat–Raymond (2611.06245) and this ledger classify it as conditional on H7/8. The Observatory's own audit (research/exploratory/riemann-observatory/audits/lean_replay/README.md) records the 7/8 theorem as 'announced with a claimed formalization, formalization not independently replayed'. quantity: Generalized constant for quadratic Dirichlet L-functions (Stopple's Λ_Kr)
statement: Λ_Kr = sup{Λ_{−D} : −D fundamental} for the heat deformation of quadratic Dirichlet L-functions L(s, χ_{−D}). For t ≥ Λ_Kr all of these L-functions have only critical-line zeros. Under GRH, Λ_Kr ≤ 0, and Stopple conjectures 0 ≤ Λ_Kr. Theorem 3: −D = −175990483 satisfies the low-discriminant criterion (15), so −1.12929×10⁻⁷ < Λ_Kr. Theorem 2: infinitely many discriminants satisfying (15) would imply 0 ≤ Λ_Kr, which random matrix theory predicts.
value: Λ_Kr > −1.12929×10⁻⁷ (superseded by Dobner: Λ_χ ≥ 0 for each primitive χ)
location: Theorem 3, p.18. Theorem 2, p.14. Definition of Λ_Kr, p.~5.

quantity: Non-trivial upper bounds Λ_L < 1/2 for Dirichlet L-functions (real primitive characters)
statement: Theorem 1.1: let χ_m be a primitive real character with conductor 3 ≤ m ≤ 400, and suppose every zero z of H_0^L satisfies |Im z| ≤ D for some 0 < D ≤ 1. Then Λ_L ≤ min(D²/2, Λ*(m, χ_m; D)), where Λ* is the infimum of t0 + y0²/2 over verified admissible triples. With D = 1 (unconditional): Λ_L ≤ 953/3200 = 0.2978125 for every such character, with stronger individual bounds in the appendix. The method extends Polymath's effective approximation with explicit conductor dependence and uses Platt's GRH verification to height h_m = 10⁸/m. Results for D < 1 are conditional, e.g. D = 3/4 under the 7/8 half-plane.
value: Λ_L ≤ 0.2978125 for all real primitive χ with conductor 3 ≤ m ≤ 400 (claimed)
location: Theorem 1.1, p.5. Remark 3.1 (initial-strip hypotheses). §6.10 (proof of Thm 1.1). §7 (numerics).
caveats: Unrefereed. The authors say these are the first non-trivial upper bounds for a Dirichlet L-function; before this only de Bruijn's 1/2 was known. The bounds are weaker than for ζ because the GRH verification height (10⁸/m) is far below 3·10¹². Nothing is claimed for complex characters or for conductors above 400. I did not replay the interval computations.

quantity: Newman constants for function-field L-functions
statement: Over F_q[T], RH (Weil) gives Λ_D ≤ 0 for every quadratic L(s, χ_D), and Λ_D can equal −∞. Newman's conjecture is therefore replaced by a family version, sup_{D∈F} Λ_D = 0. Andrade–Chang–Miller Thm 1.9: for squarefree D ∈ Z[T] of degree 3, Λ_{D_p} = log(|a_p(D)| / (2√p)), and Sato–Tate (non-CM case) gives sup_p Λ_{D_p} = 0. They also show that the Lehmer-pair lower-bound technique is insufficient for linear combinations of L-functions. Chang–Mehrle–Miller–Reiter–Stahl–Yott Thm 1.7: for q an odd prime power and a family F of monic squarefree D of odd degree ≥ 3 with (x^q − x, q) ∈ F, sup Λ_D = max Λ_D = 0, attained because Λ_D = 0 iff the L-function has a double root.
value: Λ_D ∈ [−∞, 0]; family supremum = 0 (attained for the families above)
location: ACM Conjecture 1.8 and Theorem 1.9, p.4. Chang et al. Theorem 1.7 and Corollary 1.8, p.3.
caveats: I did not verify the journal publication of Chang et al. In function fields an individual L-function can have Λ_D < 0, so the individual Newman statement can fail. This contrasts with Dobner's Λ_F ≥ 0 for every F ∈ S♯ over number fields.

quantity: Total positivity of the de Bruijn–Newman kernel (negative result)

Eight further configurations are certified by two methods. The lower determinants D_2, D_3, D_4 are positive at the central configuration, but this does not establish PF_4 globally.

quantity: Analogue of Λ for the integral of ξ (a functional-equation family with no finite constant)
statement: For a one-parameter family of Fourier integrals satisfying a functional equation, which includes the integral of the Riemann ξ-function, members have only finitely many zeros on the critical line, and the zeros lie arbitrarily far from it. The de Bruijn–Newman analogue for this family is infinite.
location: Abstract (main theorems not located in full text).
caveats: This is a cautionary example: a functional equation alone does not give a finite constant, because de Bruijn's bound needs an initial zero strip. Dobner's S♯ framework supplies that strip through the Dirichlet-series axioms.

quantity: Explicit Weyl-type bound |zeta(1/2+it)| <= C t^{1/6} log t (record refereed constant)
statement: For all real t >= 3, |zeta(1/2+it)| <= 0.618 t^{1/6} log t. The proof covers four ranges. (a) 3<=t<200: the interval-arithmetic computation of Hiary 2016 gives constant 0.595. (b) 200<=t<5.5e7: Riemann-Siegel-Lehman bound plus triangle inequality. (c) 5.5e7<=t<1e12: explicit van der Corput A/B processes with phi=0.3414, r0=4, eta=1.8. (d) t>=1e12: phi=1/3. The proof uses a generalized Kusmin-Landau lemma with the correct constant 2/pi.
location: Theorem 1.1, p.2; §3.1-§3.4 (eqs. 3.13-3.15 and the displayed range inequalities in §3.3); arXiv v1 (6 Jul 2022) read

history.note: Their Lemma 2 (Kusmin-Landau) has the wrong constant 1/pi instead of 2/pi
Invalid as stated: relies on the faulty Cheng-Graham lemma (HSW 2022 footnote 4; HPY)
Corrected value is 0.77 after the 2/pi fix (HPY, p.1)

caveats: ERRATUM CHAIN: Cheng-Graham 2004, Lemma 2, gives S <= 1/(pi theta)+1, but the sharp Kusmin-Landau constant is 2/pi (Kusmin 1927; Landau 1928). The error was pointed out by K. Ford and in a preprint of J. Arias de Reyna (HPY p.1). HPY state that it 'impacted all published explicit subconvex bounds on |zeta(1/2+it)|', including Hiary's 0.63 (corrected to 0.77) and Platt-Trudgian's 0.732. BARRIERS: max_{t>=3} |zeta(1/2+it)|/(t^{1/6} log t) > 0.507 (Hiary), quoted as >0.5075 near t = 45.62, 63.06, 108.99 by Revers. So no constant below about 0.5075 can hold for all t >= 3. Any proof that uses the Riemann-Siegel-Lehman bound on some range cannot go below 0.541. MY CHECK (non-rigorous mpmath recomputation): the three displayed inequalities in HPY §3.3 hold on their stated ranges with minimum relative slack 6.0e-5, 7.2e-6 and 4.3e-2. Revers 2026 says HPY omits some details, but he does not allege an error.

quantity: Claimed improvement of the explicit Weyl constant (unrefereed)
statement: Claimed: (a) |zeta(1/2+it)| <= 0.611 t^{1/6} log t for t >= 3; (b) |zeta(1/2+it)| <= 0.566 t^{1/6} log t for t >= 8.97e17. Regions: 3<=t<=200 (Hiary's interval arithmetic); 200<=t<=3.8e7; a 'bottleneck' range 3.8e7<=t<=8.97e17 split into 10 subregions with tuned (c, phi); and t >= 8.97e17.
caveats: MY CHECK (non-rigorous, mpmath with 30-40 digits, using the printed 6-significant-digit coefficients): the ten §3.4 inequalities a1 t^{1/6}log t - a2 t^{1/6} + a3 t^{phi/2} - a4 <= 0.611 t^{1/6} log t have minimum relative slack between -5.0e-7 and +1.1e-5. Three subregions show tiny negative slack with the printed coefficients: [4.43e7, 4.96e7] (-5.0e-7 at t=4.96e7), [5.82e7, 7.06e7] (-3.5e-8) and [3.92e8, 8.97e17] (-7.1e-9). This is within the rounding of the printed coefficients, so it is not evidence of an error. It does show the claimed constant has essentially zero numerical margin. Validating the claim needs the unrounded coefficients and directed-rounding (interval) evaluation, which I did not do. For comparison, HPY's displayed inequalities have slack >= 7.2e-6. The improvement over 0.618 is about 1.1%.

quantity: Explicit sub-Weyl bound for |zeta(1/2+it)|
statement: For t >= 3, |zeta(1/2+it)| <= 66.7 t^{27/164}. Theorem 1.1 alone is the sharpest known explicit bound for t >= exp(105); with the refinements of §3.1, Patel-Yang's bounds are the sharpest for t >= exp(61). Below that, 0.618 t^{1/6} log t is sharper, including near t ≈ 3e12, the height to which RH has been verified.

No explicit (effective-constant) version of Bombieri-Iwaniec 9/56, Huxley 32/205 or Bourgain 13/84 is recorded. This bound is used downstream, e.g. by Bellotti-Wong for t > exp(105).

quantity: RH-conditional upper bound for log|zeta(1/2+it)| (leading constant)
statement: Assume RH. As t -> infinity, log|zeta(1/2+it)| <= (log 2/2) log t/log log t + O(log t log log log t/(log log t)^2) (Chandee-Soundararajan Thm 1.1). The error was later sharpened to O(log t/(log log t)^2) (as cited by Carneiro-Milinovich 2024). Carneiro-Milinovich 2024, Theorem 2 (RH, t>=10, any integer K>=4) adds a second-order term: log|zeta(1/2+it)| <= (log 2/2) log t/log log t + (log 2/2 + log^2 2) log t/(log log t)^2 + (third-order term) + sum_{k=4}^K C_k log t/(log log t)^k + O_K(log t/(log log t)^{K+1}).
location: CS Theorem 1.1, p.1-2; refinement: Carneiro-Milinovich, arXiv 2403.17803, Theorem 2 and eq. (1.2)

history.value: |zeta(1/2+it)| << exp(C log t/log log t), some C
any C > (1+lambda0)/4 = 0.372..., where lambda0 = 0.4912... solves e^{-lambda}=lambda+lambda^2/2
Same leading constant; explicit lower-order terms

caveats: CS describe their result as the optimal outcome of the Guinand-Weil explicit formula combined with the optimal Carneiro-Vaaler bandlimited minorant of log((4+x^2)/x^2), with the prime sum estimated trivially. It is the 'limit of existing methods' in Soundararajan's sense. Expected truth is much smaller (Farmer-Gonek-Hughes, GROWTH-16). The third-order coefficient in CM Theorem 2 was garbled in my PDF extraction and is not reproduced here. For explicit, all-t RH bounds see GROWTH-07.

statement: Assume RH. For t sufficiently large, |S(t)| <= (1/4) log t/log log t + O(log t log log log t/(log log t)^2) (Theorem 2). Also -(pi/24 + o(1)) log t/(log log t)^2 <= S_1(t) <= (pi/48 + o(1)) log t/(log log t)^2, with o(1) = O(log log log t/log log t) (Theorem 1). Here S(t) = (1/pi) arg zeta(1/2+it) and S_1(t) = int_0^t S(u) du.

history.note: As cited in Fiori's appendix to Bellotti-Wong; not read directly

statement: Assume RH. For t >= 2pi: |S(t)| <= 0.96 log t/log log t; |S_1(t)| <= 2.491 log t/(log log t)^2; |zeta(1/2+it)| <= exp(0.995 log t/log log t) (Corollary 1). quantity: Unconditional Omega result: maximum of |zeta(1/2+it)| on long intervals
statement: Let beta in [0,1) and 0 < c < sqrt(2(1-beta)). For T sufficiently large, max_{T^beta <= tau <= T} |zeta(1/2+i tau)| >= L(T)^c, where L(x) = exp(sqrt(log x log_3 x/log_2 x)). In particular max_{1<=t<=T} |zeta(1/2+it)| >= exp((sqrt 2 + o(1)) sqrt(log T log_3 T/log_2 T)).
value: Constant sqrt(2(1-beta)), i.e. sqrt 2 for intervals [1,T]
location: Théorème 1.4 and Remarques (i)-(ii), §1.2, p.3; Théorème 1.2 (maximal Gál sum = L(N)^{2 sqrt 2 + o(1)}); definition of L(x), p.2 (arXiv v8)

history.value: Unconditional exp(c sqrt(log T/log log T)) in short intervals
exp((1+o(1)) sqrt(log T/log log T)) on [T,2T]
exp(c sqrt(log T log_3 T/log_2 T)), c < min{1/sqrt2, sqrt(1-beta)}
history.note: First log_3 gain, via large GCD sums

caveats: arXiv history: v2 corrected a quotation from Soundararajan 2008 caused by a misprint in that published paper; v6 corrected an inaccuracy in the proof of Thm 1.6 (the L-function application, not the zeta result). The authors explain that the zeta gain is only half the Gál-sum gain, sqrt2 versus 2 sqrt2, because the method links the square of the maximum to the Gál sum (Remark ii). Since Théorème 1.2 determines the maximal Gál sum asymptotically, any improvement beyond sqrt2 must change how maxima are linked to GCD sums. That last point is my inference, not the authors' claim. The result is far below the conjectured truth exp((1/sqrt2) sqrt(log T log log T)) (GROWTH-16).

quantity: RH-conditional Omega results for S(t), S_1(t) and the iterates S_n(t)
statement: Assume RH and fix beta in [0,1). Bondarenko-Seip (Thm 2): there exist c, c1 > 0 such that max_{T^beta<=t<=T} |S(t)| >= c sqrt(log T log_3 T/log_2 T) and max_{T^beta<=t<=T} S_1(t) >= c1 sqrt(log T log_3 T/(log_2 T)^3). Chirre-Mahatab (Thm 1, RH, 0<beta<1): max_{T^beta<=t<=T} ±S(t) >= c sqrt(log T log_3 T/log_2 T), so S(t) = Omega_±(sqrt(log t log_3 t/log_2 t)). Zhao 2026 (Cor. 1.2, RH): for every fixed n >= 0, max_{T^beta<=t<=T} epsilon S_n(t) >= c_{n,beta} (log T)^{1/2}(log_3 T)^{1/2}/(log_2 T)^{n+1/2} for epsilon = ±1.
value: Order sqrt(log T log_3 T/log_2 T) for S(t), with unspecified constants
location: BS Theorem 2, eqs. (4)-(5), p.3; Chirre-Mahatab arXiv 1904.11051 Theorem 1 (Bull. LMS); Zhao arXiv 2611.19383 Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 1.2

history.value: Unconditional S(t) = Omega_±((log t/log log t)^{1/3}); S_1(t) = Omega_±(sqrt(log t)/(log log t)^{3/2}) under RH
|S| gains a sqrt(log_3) factor (one-sided in sign)
Two-sided Omega_± with the log_3 gain

history.note: Unrefereed; fills the missing sign direction for odd n

caveats: The Chirre-Mahatab arXiv comment says a mistake in an earlier version was corrected and A. Chirre was added as coauthor (v4, to appear in Bull. LMS). Zhao 2611.19383 is an unrefereed preprint from 3 days before this snapshot. Inoue-Kobayashi-Toma (arXiv 2510.14309, RH) give explicit-constant extreme values of S(t+h)-S(t) for h in [C/log T, c/log log T]; I did not extract their constant. The Farmer-Gonek-Hughes conjecture (GROWTH-16) puts the truth near sqrt(log t log log t), far above these lower bounds.

quantity: Maximum of |zeta| on random short intervals: Fyodorov-Hiary-Keating upper tail
statement: There exists C > 0 such that for any T >= 3 and y >= 1: (1/T) meas{T <= t <= 2T : max_{|h|<=1} |zeta(1/2+it+ih)| > e^y log T/(log log T)^{3/4}} <= C y e^{-2y}. The bound is expected to be sharp for y = O(sqrt(log log T)).
value: Order log T/(log log T)^{3/4}; tail y e^{-2y}
location: Theorem 1, p.2 (arXiv v2)

history.value: Conjecture: max = log T/(log log T)^{3/4} e^{M_T}, with M_T converging in law and tail ~ C y e^{-2y}
history.note: Random matrix and log-correlated field heuristics, with numerics

history.value: First order: max_{|h|<=1} log|zeta| ~ log log T
Sharp upper tail <= C y e^{-2y}
Upper bound on mesoscopic intervals |h| <= (log T)^theta, theta in (-1,0]

caveats: This concerns typical short windows (|h|<=1 around a random t in [T,2T]). It says nothing about max_{t<=T} |zeta| (GROWTH-10, GROWTH-16). The proof is an iterative upper/lower barrier scheme driven by twisted second and fourth moments. Ouimet (arXiv 2611.01905, Nov 2026, unrefereed) claims Gumbel convergence in law of the recentered maximum slightly to the right of the line (sigma -> 1/2 at an explicit rate) on expanding windows |h| <= (log T)^theta, theta > 0. That is not the critical-line FHK statement.

quantity: Fyodorov-Hiary-Keating: lower tail and tightness of the short-interval maximum
statement: Theorem 1: there exists c > 0 such that for T >= 100 and 0 <= y <= (log log T)^{1/10}, (1/T) meas{T<=t<=2T : max_{|h|<=1} |zeta(1/2+it+ih)| < e^{-y} log T/(log log T)^{3/4}} <= c^{-1} y^{-c}. Corollary 1 (with Part I): for every eps > 0 there is C such that, for t in a set of measure >= (1-eps)T in [T,2T], |max_{|h|<=1} log|zeta(1/2+it+ih)| - (log log T - (3/4) log log log T)| <= C; subsequential limits in law exist. Theorem 2: for any C>0 there is c>0 such that for 10 <= y <= C log log T/log log log T, P(max_{|h|<=1} |zeta| > e^y log T/(log log T)^{3/4}) >= c y e^{-2y} e^{-y^2/log log T}, matching the upper tail.
value: Tightness at log log T - (3/4) log log log T + O_P(1)
location: Theorem 1, Corollary 1 (p.2), Theorem 2 (p.4), arXiv v1

history.value: Lower tail, tightness, and matching upper-tail lower bound

caveats: Status is marked unrefereed only because I could not confirm journal publication; the mathematics is by established authors and widely cited. Still open: convergence in law of the recentered maximum (beyond subsequences) and the precise asymptotic F(y) ~ C y e^{-2y}.

quantity: Selberg central limit theorem for log|zeta(1/2+it)|
statement: For each fixed real V, as T -> infinity: (1/T) meas{T <= t <= 2T : log|zeta(1/2+it)| >= V sqrt((1/2) log log T)} ~ (1/sqrt(2pi)) int_V^inf e^{-u^2/2} du. That is, log|zeta(1/2+it)| is approximately normal with mean 0 and variance (1/2) log log T.
location: Theorem 1, p.1 (new short proof of Selberg's 1946 theorem); Propositions 1-2

history.value: CLT for log zeta(1/2+it) (log|zeta| and arg)

caveats: This is a distributional theorem about typical t. It gives no pointwise growth bound. Gaussian behaviour beyond the standard-deviation scale is in GROWTH-15.

quantity: Large deviations of log|zeta(1/2+it)| at scale V ~ alpha log log T
statement: Arguin-Creighton 2026, Thm 1.1 (unconditional): for alpha > 0 and V ~ alpha log log T, (1/T) meas{t in [0,T] : log|zeta(1/2+it)| > V} >= K_alpha times a Gaussian tail with variance (1/2) log log T, with K_alpha >> (C alpha^2 log alpha)^{-alpha^2} as alpha -> infinity. This recovers the sharpest unconditional lower bounds for fractional moments (Heap-Soundararajan). Arguin-Bailey-Roberts 2026, Thm 1.1 (RH): for k > 0 and V ~ k log log T, (1/T) meas{t in [T,2T] : log|zeta(1/2+it)| > V} <= C_k e^{-V^2/log log T}/sqrt(log log T), with C_k = exp(e^{ck}); this recovers Harper's moment bound. The matching unconditional upper bound for 0 < alpha < 2 is due to Arguin-Bailey 2023.
value: Gaussian-order decay up to constants across the whole regime V of order log log T (lower bound unconditional; upper bound unconditional for alpha < 2 and conditional on RH for all alpha)
conditional_on: Lower bound: none. Upper bound for alpha >= 2: RH (Arguin-Bailey-Roberts).
location: AC26 Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 1.2, p.2; ABR26 (arXiv 2604.25579) Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 1.2, p.1-2

history.value: Gaussian asymptotic for deviations up to (log log T)^{3/5}
history.note: As described by AC26; hypotheses not checked

Unconditional lower bound for all alpha; RH upper bound for all k

quantity: Other L-functions, t-aspect: GL(2) Weyl barrier (distinct from classical zeta)
statement: For a fixed SL(2,Z) Hecke cusp form f, L(1/2+it,f) << t^{1/3+eps} (Good 1982, Weyl strength; extended by Meurman and Jutila). As of 2026-11-17 no sub-Weyl t-aspect bound for any GL(2) L-function is established; classical zeta is the only case where a sub-Weyl bound is known. Holowinsky-Munshi-Sharma-Streipel (arXiv 2503.00656 v1, Mar 2025) claimed L(1/2+it,f) << t^{1/3-1/174+eps} (which would also give zeta << t^{1/6-1/348+eps}). That paper was WITHDRAWN on 2026-10-09 (v2): 'An error has been identified in the section 6 of the current version where a certain degeneracy occurs. The authors are working to address it.'
location: HMSS v1, introduction p.1 ('Good's bound has so far remained unsurpassed...'), Theorem 1, p.2; arXiv abs page, v2 withdrawal comment dated 9 Oct 2026

quantity: Exponent θ in E(T) ≪ T^{θ+ε}: the error term in the second moment (k=1)
statement: Unconditional. With E(T) defined by ∫_0^T |ζ(1/2+it)|^2 dt = T log(T/2π) + (2γ−1)T + E(T), Bourgain–Watt prove E(T) = O(T^{1515/4816+ε}) for every ε>0, where 1515/4816 = 0.314576... This improves Watt's E(T) = O(T^{131/416}(log T)^{32587/8320}), with 131/416 = 0.314903...
location: Theorem 4 and the remark after it, p.1 of arXiv v1. The obstruction to going further is discussed in §6, remark (iii), p.16.

caveats: (1) Retraction. Bourgain–Watt, arXiv:1709.04340 ('Mean square of zeta function, circle problem and divisor problem revisited'), v1 (2017) claimed a short-interval mean-square exponent ρ = 7159/22824 (Theorem 1) and θ = 517/1648 for the divisor and circle problems (Theorem 2). The arXiv v2 comment (July 2023) reports a gap in Propositions 2, 3 and 1′ and says 'Theorems 1, 2 and 3 lose their status as theorems.' (2) Li–Yang (arXiv:2308.14859, Theorem 1.2) prove θ* = 0.3144831759... for Δ(x) and R(x), calling Huxley's 131/416 the previous best. So the literature does not count the retracted 517/1648. We found no paper that transfers the Li–Yang method to E(T). Whether it can be transferred, possibly giving θ < 1515/4816, is open as far as we could check. (3) Ω-results of size about T^{1/4} (Good; Hafner–Ivić) and Heath-Brown's mean-square asymptotic ∫E^2 ~ cT^{3/2} come from memory and were not verified.

quantity: Error term E_2(T) in the fourth moment (k=2), and its mean square
statement: Unconditional. ∫_0^T |ζ(1/2+it)|^4 dt = T P_4(log T) + E_2(T), where P_4 is an explicit quartic with leading coefficient 1/(2π^2). Heath-Brown: E_2(T) ≪ T^{7/8+ε}. Ivić–Motohashi: E_2(T) ≪ T^{2/3}(log T)^{C_1} and ∫_0^T E_2(t)^2 dt ≪ T^2 (log T)^{C_2}. Durkan–Palojärvi–Trudgian (preprint) prove C_1 = 10/3 (Theorem 1) and, for fixed A ∈ [0,2], ∫_0^T |E_2(t)|^A dt ≪_A T^{1+A/2}(log T)^{4A} (Theorem 2, so C_2 = 8). This replaces Motohashi's C_1 = 8 and C_2 = 22.
value: E_2(T) ≪ T^{2/3}(log T)^{10/3} (preprint). The power 2/3 is refereed (Ivić–Motohashi 1995). Conjectured E_2(T) ≪ T^{1/2+ε}.
location: §1 eqs. (1)–(3) for the history, p.1. Theorems 1 and 2 on p.2. Corollary 1 on p.2.

history.note: secondary (DPT §1; Conrey's note math/9509224 gives P_4 explicitly)

caveats: Only the log-power is new in 2025/26. The power 2/3 has stood since about 1989–1995. CFKRS (p.10) note that the conjectured O(T^{1/2+ε}) error for k=2 is known only with a smooth weight (Ivić). Ω_±(T^{1/2}) for E_2 is attributed to Motohashi and Ivić through a web-search summary. Not verified. DPT's footnote acknowledges that de Faveri–Pandey announced power savings for the moments with 4 < k ≤ 12 (see MOM-03 and MOM-04).

quantity: Power exponent e in ∫_0^T |ζ(1/2+it)|^6 dt ≪ T^{e+ε} (sixth moment, k=3)
statement: de Faveri–Pandey (unrefereed, Oct 2026), Theorem 1.1: for every T ≥ 1 and ε > 0, ∫_0^T |ζ(1/2+it)|^6 dt ≪_ε T^{5/4 − 1/60 + ε} = T^{37/30+ε}. The best refereed bound is T^{5/4+ε}. It comes from interpolating Hardy–Littlewood/Ingham's M_4 ≪ T^{1+ε} with Heath-Brown's M_12 ≪ T^{2+ε} (1978), which gives M_k ≪ T^{1+(k−4)/8+ε} for 4 ≤ k ≤ 12 (k = power).
value: e ≤ 37/30 ≈ 1.2333 (preprint). Refereed: e ≤ 5/4. Conjectured: I_3(T) ~ 42 a_3 T(log T)^9/9!, i.e. e = 1.
location: Theorem 1.1, p.1. Discussion of the classical bound in eq. (1), p.1. §1.1, p.2.

history.note: unrefereed. Main input is a new large-value estimate (MOM-05).

caveats: (1) Unrefereed and only six weeks old as of 2026-11-17. (2) The authors disclose AI use (p.3–4): 'ChatGPT 6 Astra' autonomously produced a simpler argument extending the admissible η-range in the key large-value estimate to |η| = o(W/N^2), and a refinement of that argument is used in the paper. This step needs independent human verification. (3) Iwaniec (Funct. Approx. 71 (2024) 121–125) noted that M_6 ≪ T^{6/5−δ} would beat Huxley's zero-density bound at σ = 3/4. Since 37/30 > 6/5, the new bound does not reach that threshold (Guth–Maynard, Ann. Math. 2026, improved zero density by other means). (4) Conflicting claim: Altenschmidt claims M_6 ≪ T^{1+ε} (MOM-06). It is not recognized by this paper or by the Florea survey. (5) The GL3 analogue is not classical ζ: the second moment of a GL3 L-function is known only up to T^{4/3+ε} (Dasgupta–Leung–Young), as cited on p.2.

quantity: Large values of |ζ(1/2+it)| at the critical level V ≈ T^{1/8}
statement: Let N(T,V) be the size of the largest 1-spaced subset of {t ∈ [T,2T] : |ζ(1/2+it)| ≥ V}. The classical moment bounds give N(T,V) ≪ T^ε min(T V^{−4}, T^2 V^{−12}), with the two bounds crossing at V = T^{1/8}. de Faveri–Pandey, Theorem 1.3: for V ∈ [T^{7/60}, T^{5/38}], N(T,V) ≪_ε T^{24/17+ε} V^{−128/17}. At V = T^{1/8} this gives T^{8/17+ε} instead of T^{1/2+ε}, the first improvement since Hardy–Littlewood (1923) on the measure of the set where |ζ| ≥ T^{1/8}. The underlying Corollary 1.4 covers D_η(w) = Σ_{N<n≤2N} a_n e(w φ_η(n/N)) with φ_η(x) = √x + ηx^{3/2}, |a_n| ≤ 1, N ≤ W ≤ N^{4/3} and |η| ≤ cW/N^2. For 1-spaced W ⊂ [0,W] with |D_η| ≥ V it gives |W| ≪ N^ε(N^2/V^2 + N^{3/2}W^{3/4}Υ^{1/8}/V^3 + N^{5/2}W^{3/2}Υ^{1/4}/V^5), where Υ = 1 + |η|W.
location: Eq. (2) and Theorem 1.3, p.2. Corollary 1.4, p.2. Further N(T,V) bounds in §9 (Theorem 9.1).

history.note: trace method with third powers, as in Guth–Maynard

caveats: Negative result recorded in the same paper (§1.2, p.3). With ℓ^2-bounded coefficients the mean-value bound |W| ≪ W/√N is sharp when η = 0 (a_n = N^{1/4}·1_square(n); counterexample of Guth/Cohen/Fu–Guth–Maldague). An ℓ^∞ hypothesis is therefore essential. The generic large-sieve and Halász–Montgomery bounds meet at V ≍ N^{3/4}, the same critical regime as in Guth–Maynard. For V > T^{1/8} better bounds already followed from exponent pairs (Trudgian–Yang 2025).

source.title: The sixth moment of the Riemann zeta function

quantity: Claimed Lindelöf-quality sixth moment bound (disputed)
statement: Altenschmidt (arXiv 2304.07581, v4 Sep 2023) claims a Laplace-transform bound ∫_0^∞ |ζ(1/2+it)|^{2β} e^{−δt} dt ≪ max(δ^{−(β−1)/2−ε}, δ^{−1−ε}, ...) as δ → 0+ for β ≥ 2. As a consequence it claims ∫_0^T |ζ(1/2+it)|^6 dt ≪_ε T^{1+ε}.
location: Abstract and introduction, p.1 of v4
caveats: Treat as unverified and almost certainly not a theorem. (a) The author's own arXiv comment on v4 reads: 'Typos fixed. Additional references. Temporary version. Still need to be fixed.' (b) Later expert literature ignores it. de Faveri–Pandey (2026) state that T^{5/4+ε} had been the best known sixth-moment bound since Heath-Brown 1978. Florea's survey (J. LMS 2026) does not mention it. (c) The claim would be far stronger than the 2026 result, and would beat Iwaniec's 6/5 zero-density threshold by a wide margin. We did not locate the specific error. Recorded only so the claim is not mistaken for an established result.

source.title: Sharp upper bound for the sixth moment of the Riemann zeta function on the critical line

quantity: Range of real k for which ∫_T^{2T}|ζ(1/2+it)|^{2k}dt ≪ T(log T)^{k^2} holds unconditionally
statement: Heap–Radziwiłł–Soundararajan, Theorem 1: let 0 ≤ k ≤ 2. Then for T ≥ 10, I_k(T) = ∫_T^{2T} |ζ(1/2+it)|^{2k} dt ≪ T(log T)^{k^2}. The proof uses the Radziwiłł–Soundararajan upper-bound principle together with the fourth moment twisted by short Dirichlet polynomials (Hughes–Young or BBLR).
value: 0 ≤ k ≤ 2 (all real k in this range)
location: Abstract and Theorem 1, pp.1–2
caveats: No unconditional sharp upper bound is known for any k > 2. Arguin–Bailey (2023) proved unconditional large-deviation upper bounds for the corresponding range 0 < α < 2 (cited in Arguin–Bailey–Roberts 2026). Heap–Soundararajan Corollary 1 combines HRS with their lower bound: T(log T)^{k^2} ≫ I_k(T) ≫ kT(log T)^{k^2} uniformly for (log T)^{−1/2} ≤ k ≤ 2.

source.authors: W. Heap, M. Radziwiłł, K. Soundararajan
source.title: Sharp upper bounds for fractional moments of the Riemann zeta function

quantity: Sharp conditional upper bound for all k ≥ 0, and its implicit constant
statement: Harper, Theorem 1: assume RH and let k ≥ 0 be fixed. Then for all large T, ∫_T^{2T} |ζ(1/2+it)|^{2k} dt ≪_k T(log T)^{k^2}. The implicit constant has the form e^{e^{O(k)}} (§6). Tao (2024, preprint), Theorem 1.1: under RH the constant can be taken as e^{e^{18.63k}}, with an absolute implicit constant. Arguin–Bailey–Roberts (2026, preprint), Theorem 1.1: under RH, for k > 0 and V ~ k log log T, (1/T)·meas{t ∈ [T,2T] : log|ζ(1/2+it)| > V} ≤ C_k e^{−V^2/log log T}/√(log log T) with C_k = exp(e^{ck}). This recovers Harper's bound (Corollary 1.2).
value: order T(log T)^{k^2} for all k ≥ 0 under RH. Constant e^{e^{18.63k}} (Tao). Random-matrix prediction: constant of size about e^{−k^2 log k}.
location: Theorem 1, p.1. §6 'Remarks on the implicit constant', p.17. Tao arXiv:2407.20023 Theorem 1.1, p.1. ABR arXiv:2604.25579 Theorem 1.1, p.2.

history.value: T(log T)^{k^2+ε} for all k > 0 on RH
sharp for k < 2.181 (2 < k < 2+2/11) on RH
history.note: uses the Hughes–Young twisted fourth moment

history.value: sharp for all k ≥ 0 on RH, constant e^{e^{O(k)}}

history.note: unrefereed. Matching lower bound by Arguin–Creighton 2026 (abstract only).

caveats: Conditional on RH. Harper's paper appears to be an unpublished arXiv preprint: Florea's 2026 survey cites it as 'arXiv e-prints'. It is nonetheless universally used and built upon (Curran, Ng–Shen–Wong, ABR, Tao). Every known conditional method gives a doubly exponential constant, far from the RMT size e^{−k^2 log k}. Harper §6 explains where the loss comes from.

source.title: Sharp conditional bounds for moments of the Riemann zeta function
source.venue: arXiv preprint (cited as arXiv e-print in Florea's 2026 J. LMS survey)

quantity: Unconditional sharp lower bounds I_k(T) ≫ T(log T)^{k^2} for all real k > 0
statement: Heap–Soundararajan, Theorem 1: let T be large. Uniformly for (log T)^{−1/2} ≤ k ≤ (log T)^{1/2−δ} (any fixed δ > 0), ∫_T^{2T} |ζ(1/2+it)|^{2k} dt ≥ C_k T(log T)^{k^2}. Here C_k = C_1 k for k ≤ 1 and C_k = (C_2 k^2 log(ek))^{−k^2} for absolute constants C_1, C_2 > 0. The result is new for 0 < k < 1, since k ≥ 1 was due to Radziwiłł–Soundararajan (2013).
value: all real k > 0, with uniformity in k
location: Theorem 1, p.1. Corollaries 1 and 2, p.2.

history.value: 2k a positive integer; all k ≥ 0 on RH; unconditional with a (log log T)^{−c_k} loss for k ≥ 1/2
all rational k ≥ 0; all k on RH
alternative proofs via large-deviation lower bounds in Selberg's CLT

caveats: Laurinčikas proved I_k ~ T(log T)^{k^2} in the range c(log log T)^{−1/2} ≤ k = o(1), as cited by HS on p.1–2. The lower-bound problem for the order of magnitude is solved. Matching the conjectured constants is not: see MOM-10.

source.title: Lower bounds for moments of zeta and L-functions revisited

quantity: Explicit unconditional lower-bound constants for integer moments (vs. conjectured g_k)
statement: Durkan–Page (unrefereed), Theorem 1: ∫_0^T |ζ(1/2+it)|^6 dt ≥ (34.4+o(1)) c_3 T(log T)^9, where c_k = a_k/(k^2)! (Soundararajan's normalization), compared with the conjectured 42 c_3. The sharper value 34.4012... is computed on p.45. Theorem 2: ∫_0^T |ζ′|^6 ≥ (0.549+o(1)) c_3 T(log T)^{15}, against Hughes' conjectured 0.71948... c_3. Corollary 12: Soundararajan's 1995 bounds M_4 ≥ 410 c_4, M_5 ≥ 6484 c_5 and M_6 ≥ 56260 c_6 (M_k = 2k-th moment) become unconditional (previously conditional on Lindelöf). Theorem 10 gives improved bounds for 7 ≤ k ≤ 11; Soundararajan's earlier bounds there were 2 c_k T(log T)^{k^2}.
value: I_3(T) ≥ (34.40+o(1)) c_3 T(log T)^9, about 82% of the conjectured 42 c_3. I_4(T) ≥ (410+o(1)) c_4 T(log T)^{16} vs. conjectured 24024 c_4.
location: Theorems 1–2, p.2. Theorem 10, p.3. §6 optimisation (P_24 polynomial, value 34.4012...), pp.44–45. Corollary 12, p.48.

history.value: 2c_k for k ≥ 7; 410 c_4, 6484 c_5, 56260 c_6 under Lindelöf
improved unconditional sixth and eighth lower bounds; ζ′ sixth: 0.419 c_3

caveats: (1) Computational component. The polytope integrals were evaluated in Wolfram Mathematica with exact monomial formulas. The 24-term polynomial was found by numerical search, and the bounds are 'rounded downward'. The paper does not describe interval arithmetic or certified bounds, and we did not replay the computation. The margin 34.4012 → 34.4 is small, though the quotient is reportedly an exact rational-polynomial expression. (2) The input is the BBLR twisted fourth moment with amplifier length y = T^η, η < 1/4, with the bound evaluated in the limit η → 1/4. The constant is therefore capped by the 1/4 barrier (MOM-15). (3) The paper notes that the bounds approach Soundararajan's as k → ∞. (4) Related work: Bui–Hall–Subira Jorge (arXiv 2511.14415) handle the fourth moment times the fourth power of a d_r-type amplifier of length T^{1/8−δ}.

source.title: Amplified moments of the Riemann zeta function

quantity: Conjectured leading coefficient and full main term of I_k(T): Keating–Snaith g_k and the CFKRS polynomial
statement: Conjecture (CFKRS (1.3.1)–(1.3.3)): for integer k, ∫_0^T |ζ(1/2+it)|^{2k} dt = T P_k(log T) + O(T^{1/2+ε}), where P_k has degree k^2 and leading coefficient g_k a_k/(k^2)!. Here a_k = ∏_p (1−1/p)^{(k−1)^2} Σ_{j=0}^{k−1} C(k−1,j)^2 p^{−j} and g_k = (k^2)! ∏_{j=0}^{k−1} j!/(k+j)!. This gives g_1 = 1, g_2 = 2, g_3 = 42 (Conrey–Ghosh) and g_4 = 24024 (Conrey–Gonek); the values were checked by direct evaluation of the formula. Keating–Snaith proposed the RMT factor for all real k > −1/2.

history.value: full polynomial P_k via the 'recipe', error O(T^{1/2+ε})
same conjectures via divisor correlations (series I–V)

caveats: This is a heuristic and conjecture, not a theorem, for every k ≥ 3. Even the k=2 error O(T^{1/2+ε}) is proven only with smooth weights. No errata on 42 or 24024 were found: Conrey–Ghosh, Conrey–Gonek, Keating–Snaith and CFKRS agree, and the closed formula reproduces 42 and 24024 exactly. Conditional derivations: see MOM-13.

quantity: Numerical comparison of the sixth moment with the CFKRS polynomial
statement: CFKRS Table 5.1.2 compares ∫|ζ(1/2+it)|^6 over windows [C,D] ⊂ [0, 2,350,000] with Conjecture 1.5.1.1. The window ratios lie between 0.9846 and 1.0130. Over the whole range [0, 2350000] the ratio is 1.000017. Table 5.1.3 compares smoothed moments for k = 1–4, with relative differences of 3.952e−5 (k=1), −7.6e−7 (k=2), 2.3e−6 (k=3) and 6.5e−5 (k=4).
value: ratio 1.000017 on [0, 2.35·10^6] for the sixth moment
location: Tables 5.1.2 and 5.1.3, printed p.67 (§5.1)
caveats: The paper says the 'reality' column was computed with Mathematica: ordinary floating point, not directed rounding or interval arithmetic. Table 5.1.1 itself marks some coefficients with '?' as not numerically stabilized. This is evidence for the conjecture over a finite range only. It says nothing about the asymptotic statement. Larger-height experiments (e.g. Hiary–Odlyzko, arXiv 1008.2173) exist but were not read.

quantity: Conditional asymptotics for the sixth and eighth moments
statement: Ng: a conjectural formula, with power savings, for a family of ternary additive divisor sums (correlations of d_3) implies an asymptotic formula with power-saving error for ∫|ζ(1/2+it)|^6. This makes the Conrey–Gonek heuristic rigorous under that hypothesis and improves Ivić's conditional upper bound. Ng–Shen–Wong: RH together with a quaternary additive divisor conjecture implies an asymptotic formula for the eighth moment. A key input is a sharp RH-conditional bound for a shifted moment.
value: k = 3 and k = 4 asymptotics, conditional only
conditional_on: Ng: ternary additive divisor conjecture with power savings. Ng–Shen–Wong: RH + quaternary additive divisor conjecture.
location: Main theorem as described in the abstract. Ng–Shen–Wong arXiv:2204.13891, abstract.

history.value: conditional upper bound for the sixth moment from a d_3 correlation conjecture
conditional eighth-moment asymptotic (RH + quaternary divisor conjecture)

caveats: The hypotheses (uniform power-saving asymptotics for Σ d_3(n)d_3(n+h), and its quaternary analogue) are open. de Faveri–Pandey (p.2) describe the unconditional sixth-moment problem as essentially needing a remainder better than X^{7/6} for Σ_{h∼X^{1/3}} Σ_{n∼X} d_3(n)d_3(n+h). Other L-functions, not classical ζ: Conrey–Iwaniec–Soundararajan (arXiv 0710.5176) proved a sixth-moment asymptotic for Dirichlet L-functions with an extra average over moduli and t. Results like this do not transfer to ζ.

source.year: 2016 (arXiv); journal version reportedly Discrete Analysis 2021 (memory, unverified)

quantity: Admissible length θ in the twisted second moment ∫|ζ(1/2+it)A(1/2+it)|^2 φ(t/T) dt with arbitrary coefficients a_n ≪ n^ε, A of length T^θ
statement: Bettin–Chandee–Radziwiłł, Theorem 1: if θ < 1/2 + δ with δ = 1/66, i.e. θ < 17/33 = 0.5151..., then I = Σ_{d,e ≤ T^θ} (a_d \bar a_e/[d,e]) ∫ (log(t(d,e)^2/(2πde)) + 2γ) φ(t/T) dt + O(T^{3/20+ε}N^{33/20} + T^{1/3+ε}) with N = T^θ. Off-diagonal terms contribute to the main term. Using Duke–Friedlander–Iwaniec instead of the Bettin–Chandee trilinear bound gives δ = 1/190.
value: θ < 17/33 for arbitrary coefficients. For structured coefficients: θ < 9/17 for mollifiers (BCHB) and 4/7 (Conrey 1989, mollifier-type, from memory).
location: Theorem 1, p.2. Discussion of the θ = 1 conjecture, p.2. Theorem 2 and Corollary 1 (conditional on trilinear Conjecture 1 ⇒ Lindelöf), p.3. Theorem 3 (products, θ < 1/2+1/10) and Theorem 4 (A·B with smooth A of length T^{1/2}, θ < 3/4), pp.4–5.
caveats: Erratum and withdrawal. Dong–Robles–Zeindler, 'Bilinear forms with Kloosterman fractions and applications' (arXiv:2601.00292, Jan 2026), claimed δ = 1/46. The v2 comment (5 Jan 2026) says: 'We accidentally missed a factor of L^2 in equation (2.53), which turns L^5 into L^7. The rest of the argument is still valid, but does not lead to an improved bound as claimed', and credits A. Pascadi with finding the error. The PDF is no longer served. 17/33 therefore stands. Negative results from BCR p.2: the formula fails in general for θ > 1, and the 'θ = 1 conjecture' for θ < 1 would imply Lindelöf. Recent reciprocity formulas (Khan arXiv 2401.01057; Tang arXiv 2608.14852) were seen in abstract only.

quantity: Admissible length ϑ in the twisted fourth moment ∫|ζ(1/2+it)|^4 A(1/2+it)\overline{B(1/2+it)}Φ(t/T) dt, arbitrary coefficients, length T^ϑ
statement: Bettin–Bui–Li–Radziwiłł, Theorem 1.1: for shifts α, β, γ, δ ≪ 1/log T, smooth Φ supported in [1,2], and A, B of length T^ϑ with coefficients ≪ n^ε, the shifted twisted fourth moment equals the six-term main term (two diagonal and four off-diagonal terms, matching Hughes–Young) + O_ε(T^{1/2+2ϑ+ε} + T^{3/4+ϑ+ε}). This gives an asymptotic for ∫_0^T|ζ|^4|P|^2 whenever ϑ < 1/4.
location: Theorem 1.1 and remarks, pp.2–3. Optimality remark, pp.4–5.

history.value: upper bounds for ϑ < 1/10 (Weil bound) and ϑ < 1/5
asymptotic for ϑ < 4/589, missing lower-order terms
fourth power of a d_r-amplifier, length T^{1/8−δ}

caveats: Negative result (BBLR pp.4–5). ϑ < 1/4 is optimal in the sense that assuming Selberg's eigenvalue conjecture does not extend it. With an amplifier of length T^{1/4−ε}, such results yield the Burgess-type bound ζ(1/2+it) ≪ t^{3/16+ε}, a natural barrier in other families. Going further 'without including new ingredients specific to ζ(s)' seems unlikely. BCR Theorem 4 reaches effective length 3/4 for structured products A·B, with A smooth of length T^{1/2} and B of length T^{1/4}. Motohashi's exact formula for the twisted fourth moment lacks error-term analysis (BBLR p.4).
